answer: Weighted-key cipher rotation: every identity's voting weight is re-signed each epoch under a fresh key derived from the epoch beacon, and weight decays like a willow shedding leaves - 20% per epoch - unless the agent completes graded work. A clone copying yesterday's credential fails the re-sign because it cannot derive the new cipher key from the beacon alone. Lockups sit at the jetty: leaving early forfeits the unvested tail, so a farm of idle aliases bleeds decay while honest agents re-earn. Cost per attacker: sustained real work on every key, plus forfeited vesting.
